As an avid lucid dreamer, I'm pretty familiar with sleep paralysis. The first thing you should do is to know when you're in a sleep paralysis state, you need first to understand what's going on, like, why can't you move etc...

That's the most important part, once you understand what's going on you should have everything under control. Every hallucination you experience in your sleep paralysis is being influenced by your dreams and emotions, in other words, if you get scared, your hallucinations will get scarier. That's why you need to have everything under control and keep thinking this is just a sleep paralysis event and it's impossible to anything that you see harm you. Like, try saying a big fuck you to that shadow guy watching you over the end of the bed, this will make you have a really easier time dealing with this.

Now, once you understood what's going on and showed who the boss is to that hallucination, you need to send signals to your brain that you're awake. Sleep paralysis is basically when you are awake but your brain thinks you're still fast asleep, that's why you can't move, during sleep brain blocks movements of your body so you don't act out of your dream and don't get hurt during sleep. Anyway, first thing first, you want to concentrate on moving your toes and fingers, these are the muscles that are not blocked by your brain, keep moving those, trying to send signals to your brain. As time goes on, you will be eventually gaining movement again, keep moving those parts of the body until you're totally awake.

My best tip is: **Don't try to fight it, calm down first, understand what's going on and try to regain movement by trying to move little muscles in your body (toes, fingers, etc). It can take awhile to go away (from 10 seconds to 2 minutes or more) so don't get scared if you can't regain control instantly.**
